reference: util-linux 2.41 hwclock, run by system Bash on the reference side; only option errors, which both sides report before any device access.
coverage: Guest pass 9 (G129): option-error wording and status.
Coordinator follow-up: conflicting options and --noadjfile without a mode, util-linux wording and status 1.
exclusions: Only diagnostics are covered here; the reviewed suite in suites/ covers ordinary operation.

cases.purpose: G129: util-linux hwclock reports unknown options and a missing -f/--rtc argument with getopt wording and the Try line, status 1, before touching any clock device.
cases.script:
hwclock --bogus </dev/null || echo "rc=$?"
hwclock -@ </dev/null || echo "rc=$?"
hwclock -@x </dev/null || echo "rc=$?"
hwclock --bogus=1 </dev/null || echo "rc=$?"
hwclock -f </dev/null || echo "rc=$?"
hwclock --rtc </dev/null || echo "rc=$?"
hwclock -u@ </dev/null || echo "rc=$?"

cases.purpose: util-linux hwclock rejects conflicting modes, two different actions, --adjfile with --noadjfile, and --noadjfile without --utc or --localtime with its own one-line diagnostic and status 1; an operand is reported after the options (getopt permutes it) with the Try line. Each fails before touching any clock device or adjtime file.
cases.script:
hwclock --utc --localtime </dev/null || echo "rc=$?"
hwclock -l -u </dev/null || echo "rc=$?"
hwclock -ul </dev/null || echo "rc=$?"
hwclock -r -s </dev/null || echo "rc=$?"
hwclock -a -w </dev/null || echo "rc=$?"
hwclock --show --systohc </dev/null || echo "rc=$?"
hwclock -rs </dev/null || echo "rc=$?"
hwclock --adjfile=adj --noadjfile </dev/null || echo "rc=$?"
hwclock --noadjfile --adjfile= </dev/null || echo "rc=$?"
hwclock --noadjfile </dev/null || echo "rc=$?"
hwclock -a --noadjfile </dev/null || echo "rc=$?"
hwclock --noadjfile -r </dev/null || echo "rc=$?"
hwclock --noadjfile --rtc= </dev/null || echo "rc=$?"
hwclock operand -r -s </dev/null || echo "rc=$?"
hwclock --noadjfile operand </dev/null || echo "rc=$?"
hwclock -r -s --bogus </dev/null || echo "rc=$?"
